learning_objective: 🎯 Uncover the magnetic effects of electric current, calculate magnetic fields using Biot-Savart's law, and explore forces on moving charges!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Moving charges create magnetic fields! The Biot-Savart law helps us calculate this exact magnetic field generated by a tiny piece of current-carrying wire at any point in space.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🦾 Force on a Moving Charge (Lorentz Force)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: A charge moving through a magnetic field experiences a force perpendicular to both its velocity and the field ($F = q(\mathbf{v} \times \mathbf{B})$). If both electric and magnetic fields are present, it's called the Lorentz Force.

A shortcut for finding magnetic fields of symmetric currents (like Gauss's law for electricity). A Solenoid is a tightly wound coil of wire that generates a strong, uniform magnetic field inside it when current flows.
Two parallel wires carrying current will exert forces on each other. If currents flow in the same direction, they attract! If they flow in opposite directions, they repel.

A device that detects tiny currents. A current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a torque, causing it to twist. By adding shunts or multipliers, it can be converted into an ammeter or voltmeter!

fun_activity.title: 👍 The Right-Hand Thumb Rule
fun_activity.instructions: Point your right thumb in the direction of the current flowing through a wire. Now curl your fingers. The direction your fingers curl shows the exact circular path of the magnetic field lines around that wire!

exam_tips: 📌 Be incredibly careful with vector cross products ($v \times B$). The force is always perpendicular to BOTH velocity and magnetic field.
📌 A stationary charge in a magnetic field experiences ZERO force. The charge must be moving to feel magnetism!
📌 Know the conversion formulas: To make an ammeter, attach a low resistance (shunt) in parallel. For a voltmeter, attach a high resistance in series.
quick_recap: ⭐ Electric currents produce magnetic fields, bridging the gap between electricity and magnetism.
⭐ Parallel wires with currents in the SAME direction attract, unlike parallel electric charges.
⭐ The magnetic force can change the direction of a moving charge, but it can never do work or change its speed!
